Oral medicine and dentistry · published research

Cicatricial pemphigoid

Small uncontrolled reports describe improvement in oral lesions or symptoms with PBM used alongside other care. The contribution of PBM is unknown.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Small uncontrolled reports describe improvement in oral lesions or symptoms with PBM used alongside other care. The contribution of PBM is unknown.

Summary of the Evidence

Two uncontrolled human reports are relevant: one exact-category case report and one three-patient case series indexed under oral mucous membrane pemphigoid, synonymous terminology. PBM accompanied systemic steroids in the case report. No controlled or preclinical study is listed.

Human and clinical evidence

The case report describes improved oral lesions and quality of life during laser phototherapy plus systemic steroids. The mapped case series reports symptom and lesion resolution in all three patients after an average of about 10 sessions. Without controls, PBM's independent contribution and long-term safety cannot be established (Oliveira et al., 2009; Cafaro et al., 2012). Both reports concern oral manifestations, not modification of systemic disease. The 2009 patient received systemic steroids concurrently, and the 2012 series includes only three patients without a comparison group; neither can separate a local PBM effect from medical treatment or natural symptom fluctuation. These observations may motivate study of adjunctive symptom management but cannot determine dose, durable remission, or whether PBM reduces medication use.

Primary original study: Oliveira et al., 2009, Laser light may improve the symptoms of oral lesions of cicatricial pemphigoid: a case report.. PubMed

Animal evidence

none identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Oliveira et al. report a 660 nm continuous-wave GaAlAs diode laser at 30 mW and 60 J/cm² per session, used with steroids. 660 nm is visible red. The concurrent steroid treatment and single-patient design are central to interpreting the result. A visible-red setting from this case does not establish a protocol for other pemphigoid care.

Interpretation

The observations may describe adjunctive symptom management, but they cannot assign improvement to PBM or establish dose, durable remission, steroid-sparing effect, or systemic disease modification. The very small evidence base and concurrent medical treatment make causal conclusions inappropriate.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low. Uncontrolled oral pemphigoid reports cannot separate PBM from concurrent treatment.
Publications and records2 unique titles.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The direct evidence consists of uncontrolled human reports, including a case report with concurrent corticosteroid treatment and a small mapped oral mucous-membrane pemphigoid report. Lesion improvement is described, but no comparison isolates PBM. The reports do not establish control of systemic disease, long-term remission, or a reliable treatment effect.
